children: Asian equities opened mostly lower on November 16, with Japanese and South Korean benchmarks sliding while Hong Kong futures pointed higher.
The Nikkei 225 fell 0.99%, the Topix lost 0.17% and the Kospi shed 0.33%. MSCI's gauge of Asian shares inched lower. Hang Seng futures rose 0.6%.

In India, the GIFT Nifty which indicates how the country's market could open for the day's trade, pointed to a positive start. The MSCI India gauge has rebounded 11% from its October low, adding more than $400 billion in value and almost erasing this year's losses, as the country's limited AI exposure has become an advantage according to a Bloomberg report.

The Japanese yen, meanwhile, was little changed at 159.67 per dollar and the offshore yuan at 6.6721. Data on Monday showed that Japan's economy contracted for the first time in a year as bad weather hit consumer spending. China's retail sales and industrial production figures are due.

Wall Street futures pointed to a tentative recovery after a weak end to last week as Nasdaq 100 contracts gained 0.5% and S&P 500 futures added 0.2%, after both benchmarks closed lower for a second straight session on Friday. Dow Jones futures rose about 50 points, Nasdaq futures about 160 points, and S&P 500 futures nearly 20 points.

On Friday the Dow recovered almost 350 points from its lows to finish just above the flat line. The Nasdaq ended 0.9% lower as pressure on Nvidia persisted, though it still posted its best week since August.

Technology stocks drove the weakness as Nvidia capped its worst week since the April 2025 tariff selloff and lost more than half a trillion dollars in market value, while the Financial Times reported that ousted Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang was discussing a possible return to the company. The sector was also rattled by a Microsoft outage last week.

Investors now seemed to await Nvidia's results on Tuesday and Anthropic's expected listing, which they seem to see as tests of appetite for the artificial intelligence trade, additionally, US retail sales and minutes of the Federal Reserve's latest meeting also loom.

Inflation worries further seem to add to the caution as US producer prices rose 0.3% in October from September and 6.5% from a year earlier, the fastest annual pace in four years, though slightly below forecasts.

Kansas City Fed President Jeff Schmid said price pressures are running too hot, and policymakers have more work to do, citing energy costs, durable goods prices, the AI buildout and healthcare costs as per a Bloomberg report.

Oil prices, meanwhile, steadied after a two-week slide. Brent traded at $96.29 a barrel, close to Friday's level, after losing more than 2% last week, while the US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) for December delivery barely moved at $88.46. Fresh attacks in West Asia revived concerns that the physical market may stay volatile.

title: Nikkei, Kospi slide: Asian markets fall as Nvidia results, US inflation concerns keep investors cautious
